title: Stratified perfect description of the integral completed category
statement: Use the coefficient conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and schemes of [def-pc-scheme]. Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here noetherian means that $T$ has a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, finite-dimensional means a finite bound on the lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertible means that $\ell\cdot1$ is a unit in each local ring. Put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the following conditions are equivalent: (i) $K$ belongs to [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], including its compatible etale-origin witnesses; (ii) there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] such that on each stratum $K$ is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_T\otimes_A^L P$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$, meaning a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules; (iii) $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf, after a finite stratification, is pro-etale locally $A_T\otimes_A N$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $N$. These conditions also describe exactly the category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] whenever that notation is used over such a $T$, with the same completed ring sheaf and reduction functors. This full subcategory is closed under shifts, cones, standard truncations and cohomology sheaves placed in degree zero.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1; Proposition 6.6.11; Proposition 6.8.11(1),(3). Adapted to the explicitly retained compatible etale-origin witnesses and uniform reduction bounds of the DAG; those clauses must be verified, not identified by notation.

proof.text: Apply integralCompletedLocalPerfectCriterion, the separate Proposition 6.6.11 result, to identify completed uniform constructible objects with stratified perfect models. The remaining argument proves the cohomology characterization of Proposition 6.8.11(3).

Construct canonical derived restriction comparisons with exact inverse image and exact slice restriction. Exact realization and restriction commute with homology. For a perfect algebra complex, cycles are submodules of finite modules and its cohomology is their quotient, hence finite and Noetherian finitely presented. Apply these comparisons to the same local perfect models, obtaining stratified finitely presented cohomology. For global boundedness, use a finite refinement of each cover on the quasi-compact Noetherian stratum, bound the finitely many perfect complexes, and take the negative sum and positive sum of the absolute endpoints. Outside this common window all local homology is zero. Cover detection gives zero on each stratum. The underlying abelian inverse-image comparison and finite-stratum detection give zero globally. This also covers an empty scheme or an empty cover.

For a finitely presented local module over the integral PID, choose a surjection from a finite free module. Its kernel is finite by Noetherianity and free since it is a submodule of a free module over a PID. In the standard localization, the thick subcategory generated by the ring contains all finite free modules, their isomorphic kernel, and therefore the cokernel via its short-exact-sequence triangle. The proved perfect/classical-generator equality makes the module in degree zero perfect. Exact completed realization, inverse image, and slice restriction transport this model to the sheaf in degree zero. No degree-zero clause is postponed.

For bounded K with stratified finitely presented cohomology, the degree-zero result and the completed criterion put every cohomology sheaf in the uniform complete triangulated subcategory. Its isomorphism closure and all shifts come from pbcIntegralUniformComplete_isTriangulated. Apply the proved source-library prop_of_bounded, which performs finite Postnikov induction. This puts K in the completed category; the completed criterion then makes K stratified perfect. This completes the second equivalence without any unproved gluing theorem.

For the detailed integral notation, use it only under its own coefficient hypotheses and with the same completed ring and reduction functors. The finite-torsion and intrinsic pro-etale constructibility definitions both ask for a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata on which the sheaf is pro-etale locally constant with finite stalks; locally closed strata of $T$ are constructible as in step 5. Membership in (i) implies levelwise finite-torsion constructibility and the uniform interval, hence the reduction conditions of the detailed definition. Intrinsic completeness is the quotient completion condition by the constant-completion equivalence, and its Roos triangle supplies the completeness condition of the detailed definition. Conversely a detailed object has intrinsically constructible finite-level cohomology and the stipulated common interval. Its completeness Roos triangle identifies its underlying object with the quotient derived limit. The latter is the Koszul completion object and is intrinsically complete by the completion-reflector lemma; completeness is invariant under isomorphism. This argument only needs the object identification and does not assert uniqueness of a lift of its projection maps. Normalized constructible local effectivity gives the required uniform tower models, and the full-faithfulness lifting argument in step 6 gives compatible etale witnesses. Thus it belongs to (i). No equality between the constant and completed ambient module categories is used.

proof.text: The uniform-complete triangulated lemma gives shifts and cones. For truncations, use the equivalence of (i) and (iii) already established in integralStratifiedPerfectCharacterization. The permitted local-module property Q is invariant under isomorphism by composing each local realization isomorphism with the inverse image of the given sheaf isomorphism. If K has bounds [a,b], the zero cohomology sheaf H^(b+1)(K) satisfies Q, so Q contains zero. The existing DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_truncLE and homologyProperty_truncGE lemmas give Q for all cohomology sheaves of both truncations. Both truncations retain bounds [a,b], including cutoffs outside the interval. Apply (iii) implies (i). Thus the parent proves truncation closure directly, without the standalone truncation split and without commuting truncations with finite coefficient reductions. For the cohomology clause, H^q(K)[0] has bounds [0,0], its degree-zero cohomology is H^q(K), and every other degree is zero. The same isomorphism and zero closure proves (iii), hence (i), directly. This removes the dependency on the companion homology theorem and avoids a cycle when that theorem uses this truncation clause.
